headword: {歴史|れきし}を{紐解|ひもと}く
gloss: to look back at history; to delve into history; to explore the past

definitions.gloss: to examine the background of a subject by tracing it through history; to delve into or explore history
definitions.explanation: A literary, somewhat formal phrase meaning to investigate or narrate the historical background of a person, place, institution, or subject. Literally "to unbind (the cords of) history." The verb {紐解|ひもと}く comes from the old practice of untying the silk cord that held an ancient scroll or book shut in order to read it; the phrase therefore evokes the image of opening up history to examine it closely. Common in magazine articles, documentaries, book titles, and guided tours.

examples.japanese: {歴史|れきし}を{紐解|ひもと}く。
{日本|にほん}の{茶道|さどう}の{歴史|れきし}を{紐解|ひもと}いてみよう。
examples.english: Let's delve into the history of the Japanese tea ceremony.

examples.japanese: この{街|まち}の{歴史|れきし}を{紐解|ひもと}いていくと、{意外|いがい}な{事実|じじつ}が{次々|つぎつぎ}と{見|み}えてきた。
examples.english: As we delved into the history of this town, one surprising fact after another came to light.

examples.japanese: {番組|ばんぐみ}の{冒頭|ぼうとう}で、ナレーターは{日本|にほん}の{自動車|じどうしゃ}{産業|さんぎょう}の{歴史|れきし}を{紐解|ひもと}き{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: At the start of the program, the narrator began tracing the history of Japan's automobile industry.

notes:
Literally "to untie (the cord of) history." Composed of {歴史|れきし} (history) + を (object marker) + {紐解|ひもと}く (to unbind, to open a scroll, to read). The verb {紐解|ひもと}く is an older, literary verb originally meaning "to untie the silk cord of a book or scroll in order to open and read it." From this came the modern figurative meaning "to investigate or explore in depth."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {歴史|れきし}を{紐解|ひもと}く: to trace / explore history
- {歴史|れきし}を{紐解|ひもと}くと: as one looks back through history, ...
- {歴史|れきし}を{紐解|ひもと}いてみる: to try delving into history
- {記録|きろく}を{紐解|ひもと}く: to go through the records
- {過去|かこ}を{紐解|ひもと}く: to delve into the past

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {歴史|れきし}を{振|ふ}り{返|かえ}る: to look back on history — a close synonym, plainer and more neutral in tone.
- {歴史|れきし}を{辿|たど}る: to trace the course of history — emphasizes following the chain of events.
- {歴史|れきし}を{掘|ほ}り{下|さ}げる: to dig deeper into history — emphasizes thorough, analytical investigation.
- {歴史|れきし}を{遡|さかのぼ}る: to go back up through history — emphasizes moving from the present toward the past.

USAGE AND REGISTER:
Literary and somewhat formal. Particularly common in:
- Newspaper and magazine essays
- TV documentaries and their narration
- Museum exhibition texts and audio guides
- Book titles, lecture titles, and travel-guide headings

In casual conversation, speakers more often say {歴史|れきし}を{見|み}ていく ("let's look at the history") or {歴史|れきし}を{調|しら}べる ("to look into the history"). The verb {紐解|ひもと}く gives the phrase a cultured, slightly elegant flavor.

NOTE ON THE VERB FORM:
{紐解|ひもと}く is also written {繙|ひもと}く with the single kanji {繙|ひもと} in literary contexts. Either form is correct; {紐解|ひもと}く is more common in modern writing.
